name: Mantua and Sabbioneta
description: In Lombardy, northern Italy, Mantua and Sabbioneta are two Renaissance towns ruled by the Gonzaga family. Mantua grew organically over centuries, and its streets still hold an 11th-century rotunda and a Baroque theatre. About 30 km away, Sabbioneta was built in the late 1500s as an "ideal city" on a neat right-angle grid, planned and finished within a single generation.
